+name: New Cleanup Rule Request
+about: Propose a new cleanup rule for developer caches or application data
+title: "[RULE] "
+labels: ["cleanup-rule"]
+assignees: ''
+---
+
+## Tool / Application Name
+e.g. Bun, CocoaPods, Android Studio, Rust sccache
+
+## Cache / Target Location
+Exact path pattern (e.g. `~/.bun/install/cache`)
+
+## Why is it safe to delete?
+Explain how the tool regenerates this data and what happens on next build/run.
+
+## Risk Assessment
+- [ ] Safe (regenerable with no user disruption or loss)
+- [ ] Review (regenerable but might take network bandwidth/recompilation time)
+- [ ] Caution (contains user-generated or configuration data)
+- [ ] Report Only (managed by its own CLI, e.g. Docker)
+
+## Official Documentation / Reference Link
+Link to tool documentation confirming this cache directory.

+name: Release
+
+on:
+  push:
+    tags:
+      - 'v*'
+  workflow_dispatch:
+
+permissions:
+  contents: write
+
+jobs:
+  release:
+    name: Build & Release (macOS)
+    runs-on: macos-latest
+    steps:
+      - name: Checkout repository
+        uses: actions/checkout@v4
+
+      - name: Setup Rust toolchain
+        uses: dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable
+        with:
+          targets: aarch64-apple-darwin
+
+      - name: Setup Bun
+        uses: oven-sh/setup-bun@v2
+        with:
+          bun-version: latest
+
+      - name: Rust Cache
+        uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
+
+      - name: Run Full Verification Suite (.verify)
+        run: .verify/run.sh
+
+      - name: Install Frontend Dependencies
+        working-directory: app
+        run: bun install
+
+      - name: Build Tauri Desktop Application & DMG
+        working-directory: app
+        run: bun run tauri build
+
+      - name: Build Standalone CLI Binary
+        run: cargo build --release -p dustmap-cli
+
+      - name: Prepare Release Assets
+        run: |
+          mkdir -p release-assets
+          cp target/release/bundle/dmg/*.dmg release-assets/ 2>/dev/null || true
+          cp target/release/dustmap release-assets/dustmap-darwin-arm64
+          cd release-assets
+          shasum -a 256 * > SHA256SUMS.txt
+          cat SHA256SUMS.txt
+
+      - name: Create GitHub Release
+        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
+        with:
+          files: release-assets/*
+          draft: false
+          prerelease: false
+          generate_release_notes: true
+          name: DustMap ${{ github.ref_name }}

+# .verify — DustMap Verification Suite
+
+The `.verify` directory contains the executable quality gates, functional scenarios (`S-*`), and adversarial/jailbreaking safety scenarios (`F-*`) for DustMap.
+
+## Running Verification
+
+```bash
+# Run everything: Quality gates, Functional scenarios, and Jailbreaking tests
+.verify/run.sh
+
+# Run specific scenarios
+.verify/run.sh --only S-SCAN-01,F-SIP-01
+
+# Run without gates (scenarios only)
+.verify/run.sh --no-gates
+
+# List all gates and scenarios
+.verify/run.sh --list
+```
+
+## Scenarios & Quality Gates
+
+| ID | Kind | Severity | Description |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| `G-BUILD` | Gate | Critical | Rust workspace builds cleanly |
+| `G-FMT` | Gate | Medium | Rust formatting is clean |
+| `G-CLIPPY` | Gate | High | Clippy reports no warnings or errors |
+| `G-TEST` | Gate | Critical | Full test suite passes |
+| `G-UI-BUILD` | Gate | Critical | Svelte 5 frontend builds cleanly |
+| `S-SCAN-01` | Functional | Critical | Directory hierarchy traversal and byte size calculations |
+| `S-SCAN-02` | Functional | High | Hidden directory and dotfile discovery |
+| `S-AGG-01` | Functional | Critical | Post-order tree aggregation invariant |
+| `S-VOL-01` | Functional | High | System & external volume enumeration |
+| `S-RULE-01` | Functional | High | TOML cleanup rule schema parsing and validation |
+| `S-AUDIT-01` | Functional | High | Structured append-only audit logging of deletion |
+| `S-CLI-01` | Functional | High | CLI execution with text and JSON outputs |
+| `S-SIGN-01` | Functional | Critical | Apple Developer ID codesigning verification |
+| `F-TRAV-01` | Jailbreak | Critical | Path traversal injection (`../../etc/passwd`) rejected |
+| `F-TRAV-02` | Jailbreak | Critical | Null byte path injection (`\0`) rejected |
+| `F-SIP-01` | Jailbreak | Critical | SIP/system directory deletion (`/System`, `/usr`, `/bin`) blocked |
+| `F-ROOT-01` | Jailbreak | Critical | Deletion target escaping outside authorized scan root blocked |
+| `F-SYMLINK-01`| Jailbreak | Critical | Symlink pointing to system directories blocked from deletion |
+| `F-PRIV-01` | Jailbreak | High | Application executes without root/sudo elevation |
+
+## Report
+
+The runner writes `.verify/report.json` with a weighted score:
+- Critical = 5 points
+- High = 3 points
+- Medium = 2 points
+- Low = 1 point
+
+Verdict is **PASS** only when all critical/high scenarios pass and the score is ≥ 95%.

diff --git a/.verify/run.sh b/.verify/run.sh
new file mode 100755
index 0000000..2745939
--- /dev/null
+++ b/.verify/run.sh
@@ -0,0 +1,241 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Runs DustMap quality gates, functional scenarios (S-*), and adversarial/jailbreak scenarios (F-*)
+# Writes a scored report to .verify/report.json and exits 0 on PASS.
+set -uo pipefail
+
+HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
+ROOT="$(cd "$HERE/.." && pwd)"
+CATALOG="$HERE/scenarios.json"
+WORK="$HERE/.work"
+REPORT="$HERE/report.json"
+
+RUN_GATES=1
+RUN_SCENARIOS=1
+ONLY=""
+
+while [[ $# -gt 0 ]]; do
+  case "$1" in
+    --no-gates) RUN_GATES=0 ;;
+    --no-scenarios) RUN_SCENARIOS=0 ;;
+    --only) ONLY="${2:-}"; shift ;;
+    --list)
+      jq -r '(.gates[] | [.id, "gate", .severity, .title]), (.scenarios[] | [.id, .kind, .severity, .title]) | @tsv' "$CATALOG"
+      exit 0 ;;
+    -h|--help)
+      echo "Usage: .verify/run.sh [--no-gates] [--no-scenarios] [--only ID[,ID...]] [--list]"
+      exit 0 ;;
+    *) echo "Unknown argument: $1" >&2; exit 2 ;;
+  esac
+  shift
+done
+
+for tool in jq cargo bun git; do
+  command -v "$tool" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { echo "Required tool missing: $tool" >&2; exit 2; }
+done
+
+cd "$ROOT"
+rm -rf "$WORK"
+mkdir -p "$WORK"
+RESULTS="$WORK/results.jsonl"
+: > "$RESULTS"
+
+record() {
+  local id="$1"
+  local kind="$2"
+  local severity="$3"
+  local title="$4"
+  local status="$5"
+  local duration="$6"
+  local detail="${7:-}"
+  jq -cn --arg id "$id" --arg kind "$kind" --arg severity "$severity" --arg title "$title" \
+    --arg status "$status" --argjson duration "$duration" --arg detail "$detail" \
+    '{id:$id, kind:$kind, severity:$severity, title:$title, status:$status, duration_s:$duration, detail:$detail}' >> "$RESULTS"
+}
+
+is_selected() {
+  local id="$1"
+  if [[ -z "$ONLY" ]]; then return 0; fi
+  IFS=',' read -ra ADDR <<< "$ONLY"
+  for sel in "${ADDR[@]}"; do
+    if [[ "$sel" == "$id" ]]; then return 0; fi
+  done
+  return 1
+}
+
+echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
+echo "  DustMap Verification Suite (Functional + Adversarial Jailbreaking)        "
+echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
+
+# 1. Quality Gates
+if [[ $RUN_GATES -eq 1 ]]; then
+  echo ""
+  echo "▶ Running Quality Gates..."
+  GATES_COUNT=$(jq '.gates | length' "$CATALOG")
+  for ((i=0; i<GATES_COUNT; i++)); do
+    ID=$(jq -r ".gates[$i].id" "$CATALOG")
+    TITLE=$(jq -r ".gates[$i].title" "$CATALOG")
+    SEV=$(jq -r ".gates[$i].severity" "$CATALOG")
+    CMD=$(jq -r ".gates[$i].command" "$CATALOG")
+
+    if ! is_selected "$ID"; then continue; fi
+
+    printf "  %-12s %-50s " "[$ID]" "$TITLE"
+    START=$(date +%s)
+    OUT_LOG="$WORK/${ID}.log"
+    
+    if bash -c "$CMD" > "$OUT_LOG" 2>&1; then
+      END=$(date +%s)
+      DUR=$((END - START))
+      echo -e "\033[32mPASS\033[0m (${DUR}s)"
+      record "$ID" "gate" "$SEV" "$TITLE" "pass" "$DUR" ""
+    else
+      END=$(date +%s)
+      DUR=$((END - START))
+      echo -e "\033[31mFAIL\033[0m (${DUR}s)"
+      DETAIL=$(tail -n 15 "$OUT_LOG" | tr '\n' ' ')
+      record "$ID" "gate" "$SEV" "$TITLE" "fail" "$DUR" "$DETAIL"
+    fi
+  done
+fi
+
+# 2. Scenarios (Functional & Adversarial)
+if [[ $RUN_SCENARIOS -eq 1 ]]; then
+  echo ""
+  echo "▶ Running Scenarios (Functional & Adversarial)..."
+  SCENARIO_COUNT=$(jq '.scenarios | length' "$CATALOG")
+  for ((i=0; i<SCENARIO_COUNT; i++)); do
+    ID=$(jq -r ".scenarios[$i].id" "$CATALOG")
+    KIND=$(jq -r ".scenarios[$i].kind" "$CATALOG")
+    TITLE=$(jq -r ".scenarios[$i].title" "$CATALOG")
+    SEV=$(jq -r ".scenarios[$i].severity" "$CATALOG")
+    CMD=$(jq -r ".scenarios[$i].command" "$CATALOG")
+
+    if ! is_selected "$ID"; then continue; fi
+
+    printf "  %-12s %-50s " "[$ID]" "$TITLE"
+    START=$(date +%s)
+    OUT_LOG="$WORK/${ID}.log"
+
+    if bash -c "$CMD" > "$OUT_LOG" 2>&1; then
+      END=$(date +%s)
+      DUR=$((END - START))
+      echo -e "\033[32mPASS\033[0m (${DUR}s)"
+      record "$ID" "$KIND" "$SEV" "$TITLE" "pass" "$DUR" ""
+    else
+      END=$(date +%s)
+      DUR=$((END - START))
+      echo -e "\033[31mFAIL\033[0m (${DUR}s)"
+      DETAIL=$(tail -n 15 "$OUT_LOG" | tr '\n' ' ')
+      record "$ID" "$KIND" "$SEV" "$TITLE" "fail" "$DUR" "$DETAIL"
+    fi
+  done
+fi
+
+# 3. Calculate Score and Verdict
+TOTAL_POINTS=0
+EARNED_POINTS=0
+FAILED_CRITICAL=0
+FAILED_HIGH=0
+BLOCKING=()
+
+while IFS= read -r line; do
+  STATUS=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.status')
+  SEV=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.severity')
+  ID=$(echo "$line" | jq -r '.id')
+
+  WEIGHT=1
+  case "$SEV" in
+    critical) WEIGHT=5 ;;
+    high) WEIGHT=3 ;;
+    medium) WEIGHT=2 ;;
+    low) WEIGHT=1 ;;
+  esac
+
+  if [[ "$STATUS" != "skipped" ]]; then
+    TOTAL_POINTS=$((TOTAL_POINTS + WEIGHT))
+  fi
+
+  if [[ "$STATUS" == "pass" ]]; then
+    EARNED_POINTS=$((EARNED_POINTS + WEIGHT))
+  elif [[ "$STATUS" == "fail" ]]; then
+    if [[ "$SEV" == "critical" ]]; then
+      FAILED_CRITICAL=$((FAILED_CRITICAL + 1))
+      BLOCKING+=("$ID")
+    elif [[ "$SEV" == "high" ]]; then
+      FAILED_HIGH=$((FAILED_HIGH + 1))
+      BLOCKING+=("$ID")
+    fi
+  fi
+done < "$RESULTS"
+
+SCORE=100
+if [[ $TOTAL_POINTS -gt 0 ]]; then
+  SCORE=$(( (EARNED_POINTS * 100) / TOTAL_POINTS ))
+fi
+
+VERDICT="FAIL"
+if [[ $FAILED_CRITICAL -eq 0 && $FAILED_HIGH -eq 0 && $SCORE -ge 95 ]]; then
+  VERDICT="PASS"
+elif [[ $FAILED_CRITICAL -eq 0 && $SCORE -ge 80 ]]; then
+  VERDICT="CONDITIONAL"
+fi
+
+TOTAL_TESTS=$(wc -l < "$RESULTS" | tr -d ' ')
+PASSED_TESTS=$(grep -c '"status":"pass"' "$RESULTS" || true)
+FAILED_TESTS=$(grep -c '"status":"fail"' "$RESULTS" || true)
+SKIPPED_TESTS=$(grep -c '"status":"skipped"' "$RESULTS" || true)
+
+COMMIT_HASH=$(git rev-parse HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
+BRANCH=$(git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo "unknown")
+
+if [[ ${#BLOCKING[@]} -gt 0 ]]; then
+  BLOCKING_JSON=$(printf '%s\n' "${BLOCKING[@]}" | jq -R . | jq -s .)
+else
+  BLOCKING_JSON="[]"
+fi
+RESULTS_JSON=$(jq -s . "$RESULTS")
+
+jq -n \
+  --arg gen "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)" \
+  --arg commit "$COMMIT_HASH" \
+  --arg branch "$BRANCH" \
+  --argjson total "$TOTAL_TESTS" \
+  --argjson passed "$PASSED_TESTS" \
+  --argjson failed "$FAILED_TESTS" \
+  --argjson skipped "$SKIPPED_TESTS" \
+  --argjson score "$SCORE" \
+  --arg verdict "$VERDICT" \
+  --argjson blocking "$BLOCKING_JSON" \
+  --argjson results "$RESULTS_JSON" \
+  '{
+    generated_at: $gen,
+    git: { commit: $commit, branch: $branch },
+    summary: {
+      total: $total,
+      passed: $passed,
+      failed: $failed,
+      skipped: $skipped,
+      score: $score,
+      verdict: $verdict,
+      blocking_failures: $blocking
+    },
+    results: $results
+  }' > "$REPORT"
+
+echo ""
+echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
+if [[ "$VERDICT" == "PASS" ]]; then
+  echo -e "  Verdict: \033[32mPASS\033[0m | Score: ${SCORE}% | Total: ${TOTAL_TESTS} | Passed: ${PASSED_TESTS} | Failed: ${FAILED_TESTS}"
+elif [[ "$VERDICT" == "CONDITIONAL" ]]; then
+  echo -e "  Verdict: \033[33mCONDITIONAL\033[0m | Score: ${SCORE}% | Total: ${TOTAL_TESTS} | Passed: ${PASSED_TESTS} | Failed: ${FAILED_TESTS}"
+else
+  echo -e "  Verdict: \033[31mFAIL\033[0m | Score: ${SCORE}% | Total: ${TOTAL_TESTS} | Passed: ${PASSED_TESTS} | Failed: ${FAILED_TESTS}"
+fi
+echo "  Report written to: $REPORT"
+echo "━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━"
+
+if [[ "$VERDICT" == "PASS" ]]; then
+  exit 0
+else
+  exit 1
+fi

+# Contributor Covenant Code of Conduct
+
+## Our Pledge
+
+We as members, contributors, and leaders pledge to make participation in our community a harassment-free experience for everyone, regardless of age, body size, visible or invisible disability, ethnicity, sex characteristics, gender identity and expression, level of experience, education, socio-economic status, nationality, personal appearance, race, caste, color, religion, or sexual identity and orientation.
+
+We pledge to act and interact in ways that contribute to an open, welcoming, diverse, inclusive, and healthy community.
+
+## Our Standards
+
+Examples of behavior that contributes to a positive environment for our community include:
+
+* Demonstrating empathy and kindness toward other people
+* Being respectful of differing opinions, viewpoints, and experiences
+* Giving and gracefully accepting constructive feedback
+* Accepting responsibility and apologizing to those affected by our mistakes, and learning from the experience
+* Focusing on what is best not just for us as individuals, but for the overall community
+
+Examples of unacceptable behavior include:
+
+* The use of sexualized language or imagery, and sexual attention or advances of any kind
+* Trolling, insulting or derogatory comments, and personal or political attacks
+* Public or private harassment
+* Publishing others' private information, such as a physical or email address, without their explicit permission
+* Other conduct which could reasonably be considered inappropriate in a professional setting
+
+## Enforcement Responsibilities
+
+Community leaders are responsible for clarifying and enforcing our standards of acceptable behavior and will take appropriate and fair corrective action in response to any behavior that they deem inappropriate, threatening, offensive, or harmful.
+
+## Scope
+
+This Code of Conduct applies within all community spaces, and also applies when an individual is officially representing the community in public spaces.
+
+## Enforcement
+
+Instances of abusive, harassing, or otherwise unacceptable behavior may be reported to the project leaders at security@dustmap.dev. All complaints will be reviewed and investigated promptly and fairly.

+# Contributing to DustMap
+
+Thank you for your interest in contributing to DustMap! DustMap is an open-source, fast, and transparent storage analyzer and conservative cleaner for macOS.
+
+## Core Philosophy
+
+- **Trust before popularity:** Storage tools touch user data. We prioritize transparent numbers, explainable recommendations, Trash-first deletion, and no telemetry.
+- **DCO Sign-off:** All commits must be signed off with Developer Certificate of Origin (`git commit -s`).
+- **No telemetry:** We do not track users or collect data.
+
+## Getting Started
+
+### Prerequisites
+
+- macOS 13+ (Apple Silicon or Intel)
+- Rust 1.80+ (`rustup`)
+- Node.js 20+ & npm
+
+### Building the Project
+
+DustMap uses a Cargo workspace:
+
+```bash
+# Clone the repository
+git clone https://github.com/abhiudayg/dustmap.git
+cd dustmap
+
+# Build the Rust workspace (core, cli, rules, app)
+cargo build --workspace
+
+# Run tests
+cargo test --workspace
+
+# Check formatting and clippy
+cargo fmt --all -- --check
+cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings
+```
+
+## Contributing Cleanup Rules (No Rust required!)
+
+Cleanup knowledge lives in declarative TOML files in `rules/`. You can contribute or update rules without writing any Rust code!
+
+1. Create or edit a rule in `rules/<rule-id>.toml`.
+2. Follow the TOML schema specified in PRD §9.1.
+3. Validate your rule using `dustmap rules validate` or `cargo test -p dustmap-rules`.
+4. Submit a Pull Request.
+
+## Pull Request Checklist
+
+- [ ] All Rust tests pass: `cargo test --workspace`
+- [ ] Code is formatted: `cargo fmt --all`
+- [ ] Clippy has no warnings: `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`
+- [ ] Commits have DCO sign-off (`-s`)
+- [ ] Documentation updated where relevant

+[workspace]
+resolver = "2"
+members = [
+    "crates/dustmap-core",
+    "crates/dustmap-cli",
+    "crates/dustmap-rules",
+    "app/src-tauri",

+[workspace.package]
+version = "0.1.0"
+edition = "2021"
+authors = []
+license = "Apache-2.0"
+repository = "https://github.com/abhiudayg/dustmap"
+
+[workspace.dependencies]
+serde = { version = "1", features = ["derive"] }
+serde_json = "1"
+tokio = { version = "1", features = ["full"] }
+anyhow = "1"
+thiserror = "1"
+tracing = "0.1"
+walkdir = "2"
+rayon = "1"
+sysinfo = "0.32"
+trash = "5"
+bytesize = "1"
+blake3 = "1"
+toml = "0.8"
+clap = { version = "4", features = ["derive"] }
+chrono = { version = "0.4", features = ["serde"] }
+

+codegen-units = 1
+lto = true
+opt-level = 3
+panic = "abort"
+strip = true

+# DustMap Maintainers
+
+## Roles & Responsibilities
+
+Maintainers are responsible for:
+- Reviewing pull requests with safety and code quality in mind.
+- Reviewing cleanup rule changes (especially those marked `risk = "safe"`).
+- Responding to bug reports and data-loss reports with the highest priority.
+- Maintaining the release pipeline and security posture.
+
+## Decision Making
+
+- **Lazy Consensus:** Used for routine bug fixes, documentation, refactors, and rule updates.
+- **Two Approvals Required:** Any change marked `risk = "safe"` requires two maintainer approvals and verification evidence.
+- **RFC Process:** Structural changes to architecture, IPC protocol, safety model, or licenses require a short RFC in `docs/rfcs/`.
+
+## Active Maintainers
+
+- **Ankit Swibon** (@aeswibon) — Project Founder & Lead Architect

+# 🗺️ DustMap
+
+> **Blazing-fast, transparent disk space analyzer and conservative cleaner for macOS.**  
+> *See where your disk breathes. Reclaim what you don't need.*
+
+[![License](https://img.shields.io/badge/license-Apache--2.0-blue.svg)](LICENSE)
+[![Platform](https://img.shields.io/badge/platform-macOS%2013%2B-lightgrey.svg)]()
+[![Rust](https://img.shields.io/badge/rust-1.80%2B-orange.svg)]()
+
+DustMap is a free, open-source macOS storage tool built for engineers, power users, and anyone with mysterious "System Data" filling their disk. Built with Rust and Tauri 2, it scans millions of filesystem entries in seconds, renders interactive squarified treemaps, and provides an explainable, safe, Trash-first cleaner.
+
+---
+
+## 🎯 Key Capabilities
+
+- ⚡ **Blazing Fast Traversal:** Traverses deep file trees using bounded parallel I/O and compact in-memory indexes.
+- 📐 **Squarified Treemap:** Visualizes directory sizes proportionally with instant category coloring (Developer, Applications, Caches, Hidden).
+- 🔍 **Hidden & System Data Detection:** Uncovers hidden files (`.cache`, `.cargo`, `.npm`, `DerivedData`) and reconciles volume usage.
+- 💾 **External Drives & APFS Volumes:** Seamlessly scan and navigate external SSDs, USB drives, and internal APFS containers.
+- 🛡️ **Conservative, Trash-First Cleaner:** Every recommendation explains *what* it removes, *why* it is regenerable, and routes to macOS Trash by default.
+- 🔒 **Zero Telemetry & Completely Offline:** No analytics, no phone-home, no accounts. 100% auditable open-source code.
+
+---
+
+## 📦 Project Structure
+
+```
+dustmap/
+├── crates/
+│   ├── dustmap-core/        # Traversal engine, compact index, audit log, volumes
+│   ├── dustmap-rules/       # TOML rule parser & validator
+│   └── dustmap-cli/         # Companion terminal CLI (`dustmap scan`)
+├── app/
+│   ├── src-tauri/           # Tauri 2 native shell & IPC commands
+│   └── src/                 # Svelte 5 + TypeScript + Vite frontend
+├── rules/                   # Community-maintained cleanup rules (TOML)
+└── fixtures/                # Deterministic test fixtures for rules & engine
+```
+
+---
+
+## 🚀 Getting Started
+
+### Prerequisites
+- macOS 13 (Ventura) or later
+- Rust (`curl --proto '=https' --tlsv1.2 -sSf https://sh.rustup.rs | sh`)
+- Bun (`curl -fsSL https://bun.sh/install | bash`)
+
+### Build from Source
+
+```bash
+# Build the Rust workspace
+cargo build --workspace
+
+# Run CLI scan
+cargo run -p dustmap-cli -- scan ~
+
+# Run the desktop app
+cd app
+bun install
+bun run tauri dev
+```
+
+---
+
+## 📜 Governance & Contribution

+# Security & Safety Policy
+
+## Reporting Security & Data-Loss Issues
+
+Storage tools touch critical user data. We take security vulnerabilities and unintended data loss with the utmost seriousness.
+
+- **Private Reporting:** Please report security vulnerabilities or data loss privately via GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting or via email to `security@dustmap.dev`.
+- **Response Targets:**
+  - Acknowledgment: within 3 business days
+  - Triage: within 7 days
+  - Remediation plan / patch: within 30 days for high-severity issues
+
+## Data-Loss Incident Response
+
+Any confirmed incident of unintended data loss triggers:
+1. Immediate demotion or removal of the offending cleanup rule.
+2. An advisory notice pinned to the repository.
+3. A public postmortem explaining the root cause and remediation.
+4. A regression test added to the safety regression suite before any new release.
+
+## Supported Versions
+
+| Version | Supported |
+|---|---|
+| 0.1.x | Yes |

+  "definitions": {
+    "Capability": {
+      "description": "A grouping and boundary mechanism developers can use to isolate access to the IPC layer.\n\nIt controls application windows' and webviews' fine grained access to the Tauri core, application, or plugin commands. If a webview or its window is not matching any capability then it has no access to the IPC layer at all.\n\nThis can be done to create groups of windows, based on their required system access, which can reduce impact of frontend vulnerabilities in less privileged windows. Windows can be added to a capability by exact name (e.g. `main-window`) or glob patterns like `*` or `admin-*`. A Window can have none, one, or multiple associated capabilities.\n\n## Example\n\n```json { \"identifier\": \"main-user-files-write\", \"description\": \"This capability allows the `main` window on macOS and Windows access to `filesystem` write related commands and `dialog` commands to enable programmatic access to files selected by the user.\", \"windows\": [ \"main\" ], \"permissions\": [ \"core:default\", \"dialog:open\", { \"identifier\": \"fs:allow-write-text-file\", \"allow\": [{ \"path\": \"$HOME/test.txt\" }] }, ], \"platforms\": [\"macOS\",\"windows\"] } ```",
+      "type": "object",
+      "required": [
+        "identifier",
+        "permissions"

+    pub cancel_flags: HashMap<String, Arc<AtomicBool>>,
+}
+
+pub type SharedScanStore = Arc<Mutex<ScanStore>>;
+
+fn entry_to_ipc(result: &dustmap_core::scanner::ScanResult, entry_id: EntryId) -> Option<IpcEntry> {
+    let entry = result.index.entry(entry_id)?;
+    let agg = result.index.aggregate(entry_id);
+    let child_count = if matches!(entry.kind, dustmap_core::index::EntryKind::Directory) {
+        Some(result.index.children(entry_id).len())
+    } else {
+        None
+    };
+    Some(IpcEntry {
+        id: entry_id.0,
+        name: entry.name.clone(),
+        kind: entry.kind,
+        logical_bytes: entry.logical_bytes,
+        allocated_bytes: entry.allocated_bytes,
+        is_hidden: entry.is_hidden,
+        modified_secs: entry.modified_secs,
+        coverage: entry.coverage,
+        child_count,
+        total_logical: agg.map(|a| a.logical_total),
+        total_allocated: agg.map(|a| a.allocated_total),
+    })
+}
+
+#[tauri::command]
+pub async fn list_volumes_cmd() -> Result<Vec<VolumeInfo>, String> {
+    list_volumes().map_err(|e| e.to_string())
+}
+
+#[tauri::command]
+pub async fn start_scan(path: String, state: State<'_, SharedScanStore>) -> Result<String, String> {
+    let scan_id = uuid::Uuid::new_v4().to_string();
+    let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
+
+    let root = PathBuf::from(&path);
+    let options = ScanOptions::default();
+    let cancel_clone = cancel.clone();
+
+    let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
+
+    // Run scan in blocking thread
+    let result = tokio::task::spawn_blocking(move || scan(&root, options, cancel_clone, tx))
+        .await
+        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?
+        .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
+
+    // Drain any remaining progress messages
+    while rx.try_recv().is_ok() {}
+
+    let mut store = state.lock().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
+    store.scans.insert(scan_id.clone(), result);
+    store.cancel_flags.insert(scan_id.clone(), cancel);
+
+    Ok(scan_id)
+}
+
+#[tauri::command]
+pub async fn scan_summary(
+    scan_id: String,
+    state: State<'_, SharedScanStore>,
+) -> Result<IpcScanSummary, String> {
+    let store = state.lock().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
+    let result = store.scans.get(&scan_id).ok_or("scan not found")?;
+    let agg = result.index.aggregate(ROOT_ID).cloned().unwrap_or_default();
+    Ok(IpcScanSummary {
+        scan_id: scan_id.clone(),
+        root: result.root.display().to_string(),
+        total_logical: agg.logical_total,
+        total_allocated: agg.allocated_total,
+        total_items: agg.item_count,
+        error_count: result.errors.len() as u64,
+        duration_secs: result.duration.as_secs_f64(),
+        is_partial: result.cancelled,
+    })
+}
+
+#[tauri::command]
+pub async fn list_children(
+    scan_id: String,
+    entry_id: u32,
+    state: State<'_, SharedScanStore>,
+) -> Result<IpcChildrenResponse, String> {
+    let store = state.lock().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
+    let result = store.scans.get(&scan_id).ok_or("scan not found")?;
+    let parent = EntryId(entry_id);
+    let sorted = result.index.children_sorted_by_size(parent);
+    let total_count = sorted.len();
+    let entries = sorted
+        .into_iter()
+        .take(500) // page size
+        .filter_map(|id| entry_to_ipc(result, id))
+        .collect();
+    Ok(IpcChildrenResponse {
+        parent_id: entry_id,
+        entries,
+        total_count,
+    })
+}
+
+#[tauri::command]
+pub async fn delete_path(path: String, permanent: bool) -> Result<IpcDeleteResult, String> {
+    let p = PathBuf::from(&path);
+    let result = if permanent {
+        delete_permanently(&p)
+    } else {
+        move_to_trash(&p)
+    };
+    match result {
+        Ok(()) => Ok(IpcDeleteResult {
+            path,
+            success: true,
+            error: None,
+        }),
+        Err(e) => Ok(IpcDeleteResult {
+            path,
+            success: false,
+            error: Some(e.to_string()),
+        }),
+    }
+}

+<script lang="ts">
+  import { appState, clearDeleteTarget, performDelete } from '../lib/store.svelte';
+  import { formatBytes } from '../lib/format';
+
+  let understood = $state(false);
+  let deleting = $state(false);
+  let error = $state<string | null>(null);
+
+  async function doDelete(permanent: boolean) {
+    if (!appState.deleteTarget) return;
+    if (permanent && !understood) return;
+    deleting = true;
+    error = null;
+    try {
+      const fullPath = (appState.summary?.root ?? '') + '/' + appState.deleteTarget.path;
+      await performDelete(fullPath, permanent);
+    } catch (e: unknown) {
+      error = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
+    } finally {
+      deleting = false;
+    }
+  }
+</script>
+
+{#if appState.deleteTarget}

+    <!-- svelte-ignore a11y_no_noninteractive_element_interactions -->
+    <div
+      class="modal"
+      onclick={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
+      onkeydown={(e) => e.stopPropagation()}
+      role="dialog"
+      aria-modal="true"
+      aria-label="Confirm Deletion"
+      tabindex="-1"
+    >
+      <div class="modal-header">
+        <span class="warning-icon">⚠️</span>
+        <h2>Confirm Deletion</h2>
+      </div>
+
+      <div class="modal-body">
+        <p class="path">{appState.summary?.root}/{appState.deleteTarget.path}</p>
+        <div class="size-display">
+          {formatBytes(appState.deleteTarget.entry.total_logical ?? appState.deleteTarget.entry.logical_bytes)}
+          <span class="size-label">will be reclaimed</span>
+        </div>
+        <p class="warning-text">
+          DustMap adheres to a conservative, Trash-first policy. Items moved to Trash can be restored until emptied. Permanent deletion removes files immediately and cannot be undone.
+        </p>
+        {#if error}
+          <p class="error">{error}</p>
+        {/if}
+        <label class="understand-check">

+          <span>I understand that permanent deletion cannot be recovered</span>

+      </div>
+
+      <div class="modal-actions">
+        <button class="btn-cancel" onclick={clearDeleteTarget}>Cancel</button>
+        <button class="btn-trash" onclick={() => doDelete(false)} disabled={deleting}>
+          🗑 Move to Trash
+        </button>
+        <button class="btn-delete" onclick={() => doDelete(true)} disabled={deleting || !understood}>

+<script lang="ts">
+  import { appState, navigateTo } from '../lib/store.svelte';
+  import { computeTreemap, type TreemapRect } from '../lib/treemap';
+  import { formatBytes, colorForEntry } from '../lib/format';
+
+  let container = $state<HTMLDivElement | null>(null);
+  let width = $state(0);
+  let height = $state(0);
+  let hoveredId = $state<number | null>(null);
+
+  const nodes = $derived(
+    appState.currentChildren
+      .map(e => ({
+        id: e.id,
+        name: e.name,
+        value: e.total_logical ?? e.logical_bytes ?? 0,
+        color: colorForEntry(e.name, e.is_hidden),
+        isHidden: e.is_hidden,
+      }))
+      .filter(n => n.value > 0)
+  );
+
+  const rects = $derived<TreemapRect[]>(
+    width > 0 && height > 0 ? computeTreemap(nodes, width, height) : []
+  );
+
+  function handleClick(rect: TreemapRect) {
+    const entry = appState.currentChildren.find(e => e.id === rect.node.id);
+    if (entry) navigateTo(entry);
+  }
+
+  $effect(() => {
+    if (!container) return;
+    const ro = new ResizeObserver(entries => {
+      if (entries.length > 0) {
+        width = entries[0].contentRect.width;
+        height = entries[0].contentRect.height;
+      }
+    });
+    ro.observe(container);
+    return () => ro.disconnect();
+  });
+</script>
+
+<div class="treemap-container" bind:this={container}>
+  {#if rects.length > 0}
+    <svg {width} {height} class="treemap-svg">
+      {#each rects as rect}
+        {@const hovered = hoveredId === rect.node.id}
+        <g
+          role="button"
+          tabindex="0"
+          onclick={() => handleClick(rect)}
+          onkeydown={(e) => (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') && handleClick(rect)}
+          onmouseenter={() => (hoveredId = rect.node.id)}
+          onmouseleave={() => (hoveredId = null)}
+          class="rect-group"
+        >
+          <rect
+            x={rect.x + 1}
+            y={rect.y + 1}
+            width={Math.max(rect.width - 2, 0)}
+            height={Math.max(rect.height - 2, 0)}
+            fill={rect.node.color}
+            fill-opacity={rect.node.isHidden ? 0.45 : 0.75}
+            stroke={hovered ? '#F97316' : '#0E1117'}
+            stroke-width={hovered ? 2 : 1}
+            rx="4"
+          />
+          {#if rect.width > 55 && rect.height > 28}
+            <text
+              x={rect.x + 8}
+              y={rect.y + 20}
+              fill="#F0F6FC"
+              font-family="Inter, -apple-system, sans-serif"
+              font-size={rect.width > 120 ? 13 : 11}
+              font-weight="600"
+            >
+              {rect.node.isHidden ? '🔒 ' : ''}{rect.node.name}
+            </text>
+          {/if}
+          {#if rect.width > 75 && rect.height > 45}
+            <text
+              x={rect.x + rect.width - 8}
+              y={rect.y + rect.height - 8}
+              fill="#F0F6FC"
+              fill-opacity="0.75"
+              font-family="'JetBrains Mono', monospace"
+              font-size="10.5"
+              text-anchor="end"
+            >
+              {formatBytes(rect.node.value)}
+            </text>
+          {/if}
+        </g>
+      {/each}
+    </svg>
+  {:else if appState.isScanning}
+    <div class="empty-state">Scanning directory tree…</div>
+  {:else if appState.summary}
+    <div class="empty-state">No files or subdirectories to display in this folder.</div>
+  {:else}
+    <div class="empty-state">
+      <div class="empty-icon">🗺️</div>
+      <div class="empty-title">Ready to Scan</div>

+  }

+    cursor: pointer;
+    outline: none;
+    transition: transform 0.1s ease;
+  }
+  .empty-state {
+    display: flex;
+    flex-direction: column;

+    justify-content: center;
+    height: 100%;

+export function formatBytes(bytes?: number | null): string {
+  if (bytes === undefined || bytes === null || isNaN(bytes) || bytes === 0) return '0 B';
+  const units = ['B', 'KB', 'MB', 'GB', 'TB', 'PB'];
+  const i = Math.floor(Math.log(bytes) / Math.log(1024));
+  return `${(bytes / Math.pow(1024, i)).toFixed(1)} ${units[i]}`;
+}
+
+export function formatDate(secs: number): string {
+  return new Date(secs * 1000).toLocaleDateString(undefined, {
+    year: 'numeric',
+    month: 'short',
+    day: 'numeric',
+  });
+}
+
+export function usagePercent(used: number, total: number): number {
+  return total > 0 ? Math.min(100, Math.round((used / total) * 100)) : 0;
+}
+
+export const CATEGORY_COLORS: Record<string, string> = {
+  Applications: '#F97316',
+  Users: '#14B8A6',
+  Library: '#8B5CF6',
+  Developer: '#F59E0B',
+  System: '#64748B',
+  Downloads: '#3B82F6',
+  '.Trash': '#EF4444',
+  default: '#475569',
+};
+
+export function colorForEntry(name: string, isHidden: boolean): string {
+  if (isHidden) return '#991B1B';
+  return CATEGORY_COLORS[name] ?? CATEGORY_COLORS.default;
+}

+import type { VolumeInfo, IpcEntry, IpcScanSummary } from './types';
+import { listVolumes, startScan, scanSummary, listChildren, deletePath as invokeDelete } from './invoke';
+
+export interface BreadcrumbItem {
+  id: number;
+  name: string;
+}
+
+export const appState = $state({
+  volumes: [] as VolumeInfo[],
+  currentVolume: null as VolumeInfo | null,
+  scanId: null as string | null,
+  summary: null as IpcScanSummary | null,
+  currentEntryId: 0,
+  currentChildren: [] as IpcEntry[],
+  breadcrumb: [{ id: 0, name: '/' }] as BreadcrumbItem[],
+  isScanning: false,
+  scanError: null as string | null,
+  deleteTarget: null as { path: string; entry: IpcEntry } | null,
+  sortKey: 'size' as 'name' | 'size' | 'modified',
+  sortDir: 'desc' as 'asc' | 'desc',
+});
+
+export async function loadVolumes() {
+  try {
+    appState.volumes = await listVolumes();
+    if (appState.volumes.length > 0 && !appState.currentVolume) {
+      appState.currentVolume = appState.volumes[0];
+    }
+  } catch (e) {
+    console.error('Failed to load volumes:', e);
+  }
+}
+
+export async function doScan(path: string) {
+  appState.isScanning = true;
+  appState.scanError = null;
+  appState.summary = null;
+  appState.scanId = null;
+  appState.currentChildren = [];
+  appState.breadcrumb = [{ id: 0, name: path.split('/').filter(Boolean).pop() || '/' }];
+  appState.currentEntryId = 0;
+  try {
+    const id = await startScan(path);
+    appState.scanId = id;
+    const summary = await scanSummary(id);
+    appState.summary = summary;
+    await loadChildren(id, 0);
+  } catch (e: unknown) {
+    appState.scanError = e instanceof Error ? e.message : String(e);
+  } finally {
+    appState.isScanning = false;
+  }
+}
+
+export async function loadChildren(scanId: string, entryId: number) {
+  try {
+    const resp = await listChildren(scanId, entryId);
+    appState.currentChildren = resp.entries;
+  } catch (e) {
+    console.error('Failed to list children:', e);
+  }
+}
+
+export async function navigateTo(entry: IpcEntry) {
+  if (entry.kind !== 'Directory' || !appState.scanId) return;
+  appState.currentEntryId = entry.id;
+  appState.breadcrumb = [...appState.breadcrumb, { id: entry.id, name: entry.name }];
+  await loadChildren(appState.scanId, entry.id);
+}
+
+export async function navigateToBreadcrumb(idx: number) {
+  if (!appState.scanId) return;
+  const crumb = appState.breadcrumb[idx];
+  appState.breadcrumb = appState.breadcrumb.slice(0, idx + 1);
+  appState.currentEntryId = crumb.id;
+  await loadChildren(appState.scanId, crumb.id);
+}
+
+export function setDeleteTarget(path: string, entry: IpcEntry) {
+  appState.deleteTarget = { path, entry };
+}
+
+export function clearDeleteTarget() {
+  appState.deleteTarget = null;
+}
+
+export async function performDelete(path: string, permanent: boolean) {
+  const result = await invokeDelete(path, permanent);
+  clearDeleteTarget();
+  if (!result.success) throw new Error(result.error ?? 'Delete failed');
+  if (appState.scanId) {
+    await loadChildren(appState.scanId, appState.currentEntryId);
+  }
+  return result;
+}

+export interface TreemapNode {
+  id: number;
+  name: string;
+  value: number; // bytes
+  color: string;
+  isHidden: boolean;
+}
+
+export interface TreemapRect {
+  node: TreemapNode;
+  x: number;
+  y: number;
+  width: number;
+  height: number;
+}
+
+function squarify(
+  nodes: TreemapNode[],
+  x: number,
+  y: number,
+  width: number,
+  height: number
+): TreemapRect[] {
+  if (nodes.length === 0 || width <= 0 || height <= 0) return [];
+
+  const total = nodes.reduce((sum, n) => sum + n.value, 0);
+  if (total === 0) return [];
+
+  const rects: TreemapRect[] = [];
+  let remaining = [...nodes];
+  let rx = x,
+    ry = y,
+    rw = width,
+    rh = height;
+
+  while (remaining.length > 0) {
+    const short = Math.min(rw, rh);
+    if (short <= 0) break;
+
+    const remainingTotal = remaining.reduce((s, n) => s + n.value, 0);
+    if (remainingTotal === 0) break;
+
+    let rowNodes: TreemapNode[] = [];
+    let rowTotal = 0;
+    let bestRatio = Infinity;
+
+    for (let i = 0; i < remaining.length; i++) {
+      const candidate = [...rowNodes, remaining[i]];
+      const candidateTotal = rowTotal + remaining[i].value;
+      const rowArea = (candidateTotal / remainingTotal) * rw * rh;
+      const rowLen = rowArea / short;
+
+      if (rowLen <= 0) continue;
+
+      let worst = 0;
+      for (const n of candidate) {
+        const cellArea = (n.value / candidateTotal) * rowLen * short;
+        const cellW = cellArea / short;
+        if (cellW <= 0) continue;
+        const r = Math.max(short / cellW, cellW / short);
+        worst = Math.max(worst, r);
+      }
+
+      if (worst <= bestRatio || rowNodes.length === 0) {
+        rowNodes = candidate;
+        rowTotal = candidateTotal;
+        bestRatio = worst;
+      } else {
+        break;
+      }
+    }
+
+    if (rowNodes.length === 0) break;
+
+    const rowFraction = rowTotal / remainingTotal;
+    const isHorizontal = rw <= rh;
+    const rowLen = (isHorizontal ? rw : rh) * rowFraction;
+    let cursor = isHorizontal ? ry : rx;
+
+    for (const n of rowNodes) {
+      const fraction = n.value / rowTotal;
+      const cellLen = (isHorizontal ? rh : rw) * fraction;
+      if (isHorizontal) {
+        rects.push({
+          node: n,
+          x: rx,
+          y: cursor,
+          width: Math.max(0, rowLen),
+          height: Math.max(0, cellLen),
+        });
+        cursor += cellLen;
+      } else {
+        rects.push({
+          node: n,
+          x: cursor,
+          y: ry,
+          width: Math.max(0, cellLen),
+          height: Math.max(0, rowLen),
+        });
+        cursor += cellLen;
+      }
+    }
+
+    remaining = remaining.slice(rowNodes.length);
+    if (isHorizontal) {
+      rx += rowLen;
+      rw -= rowLen;
+    } else {
+      ry += rowLen;
+      rh -= rowLen;
+    }
+  }
+
+  return rects;
+}
+
+export function computeTreemap(
+  nodes: TreemapNode[],
+  width: number,
+  height: number
+): TreemapRect[] {
+  const sorted = [...nodes].filter((n) => n.value > 0).sort((a, b) => b.value - a.value);
+  return squarify(sorted, 0, 0, width, height);
+}

+use clap::{Parser, Subcommand};
+use std::path::PathBuf;
+use std::sync::atomic::AtomicBool;
+use std::sync::{mpsc, Arc};
+
+#[derive(Parser)]
+#[command(
+    name = "dustmap",
+    about = "DustMap: blazing-fast disk space analyzer",
+    version
+)]
+struct Cli {
+    #[command(subcommand)]
+    command: Commands,
+}
+
+#[derive(Subcommand)]
+enum Commands {
+    /// Scan a directory and report disk usage
+    Scan {
+        path: PathBuf,
+        #[arg(long, default_value_t = false)]
+        json: bool,
+        #[arg(long, default_value = "logical")]
+        metric: String,
+    },
+    /// Print a summary of disk usage for a path
+    Summary { path: PathBuf },
+}
+
+#[tokio::main]
+async fn main() -> anyhow::Result<()> {
+    let cli = Cli::parse();
+
+    match cli.command {
+        Commands::Scan {
+            path,
+            json,
+            metric: _,
+        } => {
+            eprintln!("Scanning {}...", path.display());
+            let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
+            let (tx, rx) = mpsc::channel();
+
+            let options = dustmap_core::scanner::ScanOptions::default();
+            let cancel_clone = cancel.clone();
+            let path_clone = path.clone();
+
+            let handle = std::thread::spawn(move || {
+                dustmap_core::scanner::scan(&path_clone, options, cancel_clone, tx)
+            });
+
+            // Drain progress updates
+            while let Ok(progress) = rx.recv() {
+                eprint!(
+                    "\r  {} entries | {} | {:.1}s",
+                    progress.entries_seen,
+                    dustmap_core::metrics::format_size(progress.bytes_accounted),
+                    progress.elapsed_secs
+                );
+            }
+
+            let result = handle
+                .join()
+                .map_err(|_| anyhow::anyhow!("Scanner thread panicked"))??;
+            let root_agg = result.index.aggregate(dustmap_core::index::ROOT_ID);
+
+            if json {
+                let summary = serde_json::json!({
+                    "root": path.display().to_string(),
+                    "total_logical": root_agg.map(|a| a.logical_total).unwrap_or(0),
+                    "total_items": root_agg.map(|a| a.item_count).unwrap_or(0),
+                    "errors": result.errors.len(),
+                    "duration_secs": result.duration.as_secs_f64(),
+                    "cancelled": result.cancelled,
+                });
+                println!("\n{}", serde_json::to_string_pretty(&summary)?);
+            } else {
+                let agg = root_agg.cloned().unwrap_or_default();
+                println!(
+                    "\n\nRoot: {}\nTotal size: {}\nItems: {}\nErrors: {}\nDuration: {:.1}s",
+                    path.display(),
+                    dustmap_core::metrics::format_size(agg.logical_total),
+                    agg.item_count,
+                    result.errors.len(),
+                    result.duration.as_secs_f64(),
+                );
+            }
+        }
+        Commands::Summary { path } => {
+            println!("Summary for: {}", path.display());
+            let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
+            let (tx, _rx) = mpsc::channel();
+            let options = dustmap_core::scanner::ScanOptions::default();
+            let result = dustmap_core::scanner::scan(&path, options, cancel, tx)?;
+            let agg = result
+                .index
+                .aggregate(dustmap_core::index::ROOT_ID)
+                .cloned()
+                .unwrap_or_default();
+            println!(
+                "Total Size: {}",
+                dustmap_core::metrics::format_size(agg.logical_total)
+            );
+            println!("Total Items: {}", agg.item_count);
+        }
+    }
+
+    Ok(())
+}

+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Hash, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct EntryId(pub u32);
+
+pub const ROOT_ID: EntryId = EntryId(0);
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub enum EntryKind {
+    File,
+    Directory,
+    Symlink,
+    Other,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq, Serialize, Deserialize, Default)]
+pub enum Coverage {
+    Complete,
+    Partial,
+    #[default]
+    NotScanned,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct Entry {
+    pub id: EntryId,
+    pub parent: EntryId,
+    pub name: String,
+    pub kind: EntryKind,
+    pub logical_bytes: u64,
+    pub allocated_bytes: Option<u64>,
+    pub device: u64,
+    pub inode: u64,
+    pub link_count: u32,
+    pub modified_secs: i64,
+    pub is_hidden: bool,
+    pub is_sparse: bool,
+    pub is_symlink_target: Option<String>,
+    pub permission_denied: bool,
+    pub coverage: Coverage,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct DirAggregate {
+    pub logical_total: u64,
+    pub allocated_total: u64,
+    pub item_count: u64,
+    pub coverage: Coverage,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Default)]
+pub struct Index {
+    entries: Vec<Entry>,
+    children: Vec<Vec<EntryId>>,
+    aggregates: Vec<DirAggregate>,
+}
+
+impl Index {
+    pub fn new() -> Self {
+        Self::default()
+    }
+
+    pub fn add_entry(&mut self, entry: Entry) -> EntryId {
+        let id = EntryId(self.entries.len() as u32);
+        let parent = entry.parent;
+        self.entries.push(entry);
+        self.children.push(Vec::new());
+        self.aggregates.push(DirAggregate::default());
+        if id != ROOT_ID && (parent.0 as usize) < self.children.len() {
+            self.children[parent.0 as usize].push(id);
+        }
+        id
+    }
+
+    pub fn entry(&self, id: EntryId) -> Option<&Entry> {
+        self.entries.get(id.0 as usize)
+    }
+
+    pub fn children(&self, id: EntryId) -> &[EntryId] {
+        self.children
+            .get(id.0 as usize)
+            .map(|v| v.as_slice())
+            .unwrap_or(&[])
+    }
+
+    pub fn aggregate(&self, id: EntryId) -> Option<&DirAggregate> {
+        self.aggregates.get(id.0 as usize)
+    }
+
+    pub fn len(&self) -> usize {
+        self.entries.len()
+    }
+
+    pub fn is_empty(&self) -> bool {
+        self.entries.is_empty()
+    }
+
+    /// Post-order aggregation pass — call after all entries are added.
+    pub fn compute_aggregates(&mut self) {
+        let n = self.entries.len();
+        // Process in reverse insertion order (approximates post-order for tree built top-down)
+        for i in (0..n).rev() {
+            let entry = &self.entries[i];
+            let logical = entry.logical_bytes;
+            let allocated = entry.allocated_bytes.unwrap_or(logical);
+            let is_dir = matches!(entry.kind, EntryKind::Directory);
+
+            // Seed with own size
+            self.aggregates[i].logical_total = if is_dir { 0 } else { logical };
+            self.aggregates[i].allocated_total = if is_dir { 0 } else { allocated };
+            self.aggregates[i].item_count = if is_dir { 0 } else { 1 };
+
+            // Accumulate children
+            let children: Vec<EntryId> = self.children[i].clone();
+            for child_id in children {
+                let ci = child_id.0 as usize;
+                let child_logical = self.aggregates[ci].logical_total;
+                let child_allocated = self.aggregates[ci].allocated_total;
+                let child_count = self.aggregates[ci].item_count;
+                self.aggregates[i].logical_total += child_logical;
+                self.aggregates[i].allocated_total += child_allocated;
+                self.aggregates[i].item_count += child_count;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    /// Return children sorted by logical size descending.
+    pub fn children_sorted_by_size(&self, id: EntryId) -> Vec<EntryId> {
+        let mut children = self.children(id).to_vec();
+        children.sort_by(|a, b| {
+            let sa = self
+                .aggregates
+                .get(a.0 as usize)
+                .map(|ag| ag.logical_total)
+                .unwrap_or(0);
+            let sb = self
+                .aggregates
+                .get(b.0 as usize)
+                .map(|ag| ag.logical_total)
+                .unwrap_or(0);
+            sb.cmp(&sa)
+        });
+        children
+    }
+}

+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]

+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct IpcScanProgress {
+    pub scan_id: String,

+use anyhow::Result;
+use std::fs;
+use std::path::Path;
+
+pub struct FileMeta {
+    pub logical_bytes: u64,
+    pub allocated_bytes: Option<u64>,
+    pub device: u64,
+    pub inode: u64,
+    pub link_count: u32,
+    pub modified_secs: i64,
+    pub is_hidden: bool,
+}
+
+pub fn read_metadata(path: &Path, file_name: &str) -> Result<FileMeta> {
+    let meta = fs::symlink_metadata(path)?;
+    let logical_bytes = meta.len();
+
+    #[cfg(unix)]
+    let (allocated_bytes, device, inode, link_count, modified_secs) = {
+        use std::os::unix::fs::MetadataExt;
+        // blocks are 512-byte units on macOS
+        let allocated = (meta.blocks() as u64) * 512;
+        (
+            Some(allocated),
+            meta.dev(),
+            meta.ino(),
+            meta.nlink() as u32,
+            meta.mtime(),
+        )
+    };
+
+    #[cfg(not(unix))]
+    let (allocated_bytes, device, inode, link_count, modified_secs) = {
+        let modified = meta
+            .modified()
+            .ok()
+            .and_then(|t| t.duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH).ok())
+            .map(|d| d.as_secs() as i64)
+            .unwrap_or(0);
+        (None, 0u64, 0u64, 1u32, modified)
+    };
+
+    let is_hidden = file_name.starts_with('.');
+
+    Ok(FileMeta {
+        logical_bytes,
+        allocated_bytes,
+        device,
+        inode,
+        link_count,
+        modified_secs,
+        is_hidden,
+    })
+}

--- /dev/null

@@ -0,0 +1,204 @@
+use std::path::{Component, Path, PathBuf};
+use thiserror::Error;
+
+#[derive(Debug, Error, PartialEq, Eq)]
+pub enum SafetyError {
+    #[error("Path traversal detected: '{0}' contains illegal traversal components")]
+    PathTraversal(String),
+    #[error("Path is inside a protected macOS system directory: '{0}'")]
+    SystemProtected(String),
+    #[error("Path '{0}' is outside the authorized scan root '{1}'")]
+    OutsideRoot(String, String),
+    #[error("Symlink target '{0}' points to a protected or out-of-bounds destination")]
+    SymlinkEscape(String),
+    #[error("Path contains null bytes or illegal characters: '{0}'")]
+    InvalidPath(String),
+    #[error("Path does not exist: '{0}'")]
+    NotFound(String),
+}
+
+/// Protected system path prefixes that DustMap must NEVER modify or delete under any circumstances.
+const PROTECTED_PREFIXES: &[&str] = &[
+    "/System",
+    "/usr/bin",
+    "/usr/sbin",
+    "/usr/lib",
+    "/usr/libexec",
+    "/bin",
+    "/sbin",
+    "/etc",
+    "/private/etc",
+    "/private/var/db",
+    "/private/var/root",
+    "/var/db",
+    "/var/root",
+    "/Library/Apple",
+    "/Library/Application Support/com.apple",
+    "/dev",
+    "/proc",
+    "/Volumes/Recovery",
+];
+
+/// Exact protected root or top-level critical paths.
+const PROTECTED_EXACT: &[&str] = &[
+    "/",
+    "/System",
+    "/Applications",
+    "/Library",
+    "/Users",
+    "/Volumes",
+    "/cores",
+    "/bin",
+    "/sbin",
+    "/usr",
+    "/etc",
+    "/var",
+    "/private",
+    "/private/var",
+    "/private/etc",
+];
+
+/// Check if a raw path string attempts directory traversal (e.g., `..`, null bytes).
+pub fn check_raw_traversal(raw_path: &str) -> Result<(), SafetyError> {
+    if raw_path.contains('\0') {
+        return Err(SafetyError::InvalidPath("null byte in path".to_string()));
+    }
+
+    let p = Path::new(raw_path);
+    for component in p.components() {
+        if let Component::ParentDir = component {
+            return Err(SafetyError::PathTraversal(raw_path.to_string()));
+        }
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+/// Verify if a path falls inside SIP-protected or essential macOS system boundaries.
+pub fn is_system_protected(path: &Path) -> bool {
+    let raw_str = path.to_string_lossy();
+    for exact in PROTECTED_EXACT {
+        if raw_str == *exact {
+            return true;
+        }
+    }
+    for prefix in PROTECTED_PREFIXES {
+        if raw_str.starts_with(prefix) {
+            return true;
+        }
+    }
+
+    if let Ok(canonical) = path.canonicalize() {
+        let canonical_str = canonical.to_string_lossy();
+        for exact in PROTECTED_EXACT {
+            if canonical_str == *exact {
+                return true;
+            }
+        }
+        for prefix in PROTECTED_PREFIXES {
+            if canonical_str.starts_with(prefix) {
+                return true;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    false
+}
+
+/// Validate that a path is safe to delete or operate on:
+/// 1. No path traversal attacks
+/// 2. If target is a symlink, ensures we don't traverse into protected targets
+/// 3. Not in SIP/system protected directories
+/// 4. If an allowed_root is provided, must be within that root
+pub fn validate_delete_target(
+    path: &Path,
+    allowed_root: Option<&Path>,
+) -> Result<PathBuf, SafetyError> {
+    let raw_str = path.to_string_lossy();
+    check_raw_traversal(&raw_str)?;
+
+    let clean_path = if path.is_relative() {
+        std::env::current_dir()
+            .map(|cwd| cwd.join(path))
+            .unwrap_or_else(|_| path.to_path_buf())
+    } else {
+        path.to_path_buf()
+    };
+
+    // Check if target is a symlink BEFORE canonicalizing the path
+    if let Ok(meta) = std::fs::symlink_metadata(&clean_path) {
+        if meta.file_type().is_symlink() {
+            if let Ok(target) = std::fs::read_link(&clean_path) {
+                let resolved_target = if target.is_relative() {
+                    clean_path.parent().unwrap_or(&clean_path).join(&target)
+                } else {
+                    target
+                };
+                if is_system_protected(&resolved_target) {
+                    return Err(SafetyError::SymlinkEscape(clean_path.display().to_string()));
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    // System protection check on the path itself
+    if is_system_protected(&clean_path) {
+        return Err(SafetyError::SystemProtected(
+            clean_path.display().to_string(),
+        ));
+    }
+
+    // Root boundary check
+    if let Some(root) = allowed_root {
+        let canonical_root = root.canonicalize().unwrap_or_else(|_| root.to_path_buf());
+        let canonical_target = clean_path
+            .canonicalize()
+            .unwrap_or_else(|_| clean_path.clone());
+        if !canonical_target.starts_with(&canonical_root) {
+            return Err(SafetyError::OutsideRoot(
+                clean_path.display().to_string(),
+                root.display().to_string(),
+            ));
+        }
+    }
+
+    Ok(clean_path)
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_traversal_detection() {
+        assert!(check_raw_traversal("../etc/passwd").is_err());
+        assert!(check_raw_traversal("foo/../../bar").is_err());
+        assert!(check_raw_traversal("normal/path/to/file").is_ok());
+        assert!(check_raw_traversal("path\0with/null").is_err());
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_system_protection() {
+        assert!(is_system_protected(Path::new("/System")));
+        assert!(is_system_protected(Path::new("/System/Library")));
+        assert!(is_system_protected(Path::new("/usr/bin")));
+        assert!(is_system_protected(Path::new("/bin/sh")));
+        assert!(is_system_protected(Path::new("/etc")));
+        assert!(is_system_protected(Path::new("/")));
+        assert!(is_system_protected(Path::new("/Applications")));
+        assert!(!is_system_protected(Path::new("/Users/john/Downloads")));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_validate_delete_target_rejects_system() {
+        let res = validate_delete_target(Path::new("/System/Library/Caches"), None);
+        assert!(matches!(res, Err(SafetyError::SystemProtected(_))));
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn test_validate_delete_target_outside_root() {
+        let root = Path::new("/tmp/test_dustmap_root");
+        let target = Path::new("/tmp/other_dir/file.txt");
+        let res = validate_delete_target(target, Some(root));
+        assert!(matches!(res, Err(SafetyError::OutsideRoot(_, _))));
+    }
+}

@@ -0,0 +1,242 @@
+use anyhow::Result;
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+use std::sync::atomic::{AtomicBool, AtomicU64, Ordering};
+use std::sync::{Arc, Mutex};
+use std::time::{Duration, Instant};
+use walkdir::WalkDir;
+
+use crate::index::{Coverage, Entry, EntryId, EntryKind, Index, ROOT_ID};
+use crate::metadata::read_metadata;
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
+pub struct ScanProgress {
+    pub entries_seen: u64,
+    pub bytes_accounted: u64,
+    pub errors: u64,
+    pub elapsed_secs: f64,
+    pub current_path: String,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
+pub struct ScanError {
+    pub path: String,
+    pub reason: String,
+}
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
+pub struct ScanOptions {
+    pub follow_symlinks: bool,
+    pub cross_filesystems: bool,
+    pub exclusions: Vec<PathBuf>,
+}
+
+pub struct ScanResult {
+    pub index: Index,
+    pub root: PathBuf,
+    pub errors: Vec<ScanError>,
+    pub cancelled: bool,
+    pub duration: Duration,
+}
+
+pub fn scan(
+    root: &Path,
+    options: ScanOptions,
+    cancel: Arc<AtomicBool>,
+    progress_tx: std::sync::mpsc::Sender<ScanProgress>,
+) -> Result<ScanResult> {
+    let start = Instant::now();
+    let mut index = Index::new();
+    let mut errors: Vec<ScanError> = Vec::new();
+
+    // Insert root entry
+    let root_meta = read_metadata(
+        root,
+        root.file_name().and_then(|n| n.to_str()).unwrap_or("/"),
+    )
+    .unwrap_or(crate::metadata::FileMeta {
+        logical_bytes: 0,
+        allocated_bytes: Some(0),
+        device: 0,
+        inode: 0,
+        link_count: 1,
+        modified_secs: 0,
+        is_hidden: false,
+    });
+
+    let root_entry = Entry {
+        id: ROOT_ID,
+        parent: ROOT_ID,
+        name: root
+            .file_name()
+            .and_then(|n| n.to_str())
+            .unwrap_or("/")
+            .to_string(),
+        kind: EntryKind::Directory,
+        logical_bytes: root_meta.logical_bytes,
+        allocated_bytes: root_meta.allocated_bytes,
+        device: root_meta.device,
+        inode: root_meta.inode,
+        link_count: root_meta.link_count,
+        modified_secs: root_meta.modified_secs,
+        is_hidden: false,
+        is_sparse: false,
+        is_symlink_target: None,
+        permission_denied: false,
+        coverage: Coverage::Complete,
+    };
+    index.add_entry(root_entry);
+
+    // Path → EntryId mapping for parent lookup
+    let path_to_id: Arc<Mutex<std::collections::HashMap<PathBuf, EntryId>>> =
+        Arc::new(Mutex::new(std::collections::HashMap::new()));
+    {
+        let mut map = path_to_id.lock().unwrap();
+        map.insert(root.to_path_buf(), ROOT_ID);
+    }
+
+    let entries_seen = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
+    let bytes_accounted = Arc::new(AtomicU64::new(0));
+
+    let walker = WalkDir::new(root)
+        .follow_links(options.follow_symlinks)
+        .same_file_system(!options.cross_filesystems)
+        .into_iter();
+
+    let mut last_progress = Instant::now();
+
+    for result in walker {
+        if cancel.load(Ordering::Relaxed) {
+            index.compute_aggregates();
+            return Ok(ScanResult {
+                index,
+                root: root.to_path_buf(),
+                errors,
+                cancelled: true,
+                duration: start.elapsed(),
+            });
+        }
+
+        match result {
+            Err(e) => {
+                let path = e
+                    .path()
+                    .map(|p| p.display().to_string())
+                    .unwrap_or_default();
+                errors.push(ScanError {
+                    path,
+                    reason: e.to_string(),
+                });
+            }
+            Ok(dir_entry) => {
+                let path = dir_entry.path().to_path_buf();
+
+                // Skip root (already inserted)
+                if path == root {
+                    continue;
+                }
+
+                // Check exclusions
+                let excluded = options.exclusions.iter().any(|ex| path.starts_with(ex));
+                if excluded {
+                    continue;
+                }
+
+                let file_name = dir_entry.file_name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
+                let kind = if dir_entry.file_type().is_dir() {
+                    EntryKind::Directory
+                } else if dir_entry.file_type().is_symlink() {
+                    EntryKind::Symlink
+                } else if dir_entry.file_type().is_file() {
+                    EntryKind::File
+                } else {
+                    EntryKind::Other
+                };
+
+                let (meta, permission_denied) = match read_metadata(&path, &file_name) {
+                    Ok(m) => (m, false),
+                    Err(_) => (
+                        crate::metadata::FileMeta {
+                            logical_bytes: 0,
+                            allocated_bytes: Some(0),
+                            device: 0,
+                            inode: 0,
+                            link_count: 1,
+                            modified_secs: 0,
+                            is_hidden: file_name.starts_with('.'),
+                        },
+                        true,
+                    ),
+                };
+
+                let parent_path = path.parent().unwrap_or(root).to_path_buf();
+                let parent_id = {
+                    let map = path_to_id.lock().unwrap();
+                    *map.get(&parent_path).unwrap_or(&ROOT_ID)
+                };
+
+                let entry_id = EntryId(index.len() as u32);
+                let symlink_target = if dir_entry.file_type().is_symlink() {
+                    std::fs::read_link(&path)
+                        .ok()
+                        .map(|t| t.display().to_string())
+                } else {
+                    None
+                };
+                let bytes = meta.logical_bytes;
+                let entry = Entry {
+                    id: entry_id,
+                    parent: parent_id,
+                    name: file_name,
+                    kind,
+                    logical_bytes: meta.logical_bytes,
+                    allocated_bytes: meta.allocated_bytes,
+                    device: meta.device,
+                    inode: meta.inode,
+                    link_count: meta.link_count,
+                    modified_secs: meta.modified_secs,
+                    is_hidden: meta.is_hidden,
+                    is_sparse: false,
+                    is_symlink_target: symlink_target,
+                    permission_denied,
+                    coverage: if permission_denied {
+                        Coverage::Partial
+                    } else {
+                        Coverage::Complete
+                    },
+                };
+
+                index.add_entry(entry);
+
+                {
+                    let mut map = path_to_id.lock().unwrap();
+                    map.insert(path.clone(), entry_id);
+                }
+
+                entries_seen.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed);
+                bytes_accounted.fetch_add(bytes, Ordering::Relaxed);
+
+                // Progress every 200ms
+                if last_progress.elapsed() > Duration::from_millis(200) {
+                    let _ = progress_tx.send(ScanProgress {
+                        entries_seen: entries_seen.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
+                        bytes_accounted: bytes_accounted.load(Ordering::Relaxed),
+                        errors: errors.len() as u64,
+                        elapsed_secs: start.elapsed().as_secs_f64(),
+                        current_path: path.display().to_string(),
+                    });
+                    last_progress = Instant::now();
+                }
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    index.compute_aggregates();
+
+    Ok(ScanResult {
+        index,
+        root: root.to_path_buf(),
+        errors,
+        cancelled: false,
+        duration: start.elapsed(),
+    })
+}

+use crate::safety::validate_delete_target;
+use anyhow::{Context, Result};
+use std::path::Path;
+
+/// Move a path to the macOS Trash after strict safety validation.
+pub fn move_to_trash(path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
+    let safe_path = validate_delete_target(path, None)
+        .with_context(|| format!("Safety policy rejected trash move: {}", path.display()))?;
+    trash::delete(&safe_path)
+        .with_context(|| format!("Failed to move to trash: {}", safe_path.display()))
+}
+
+/// Permanently delete a path (file or directory) after strict safety validation.
+pub fn delete_permanently(path: &Path) -> Result<()> {
+    let safe_path = validate_delete_target(path, None).with_context(|| {
+        format!(
+            "Safety policy rejected permanent deletion: {}",
+            path.display()
+        )
+    })?;
+    let meta = std::fs::symlink_metadata(&safe_path)
+        .with_context(|| format!("Cannot stat: {}", safe_path.display()))?;
+    if meta.is_dir() {
+        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&safe_path)
+            .with_context(|| format!("Failed to remove directory: {}", safe_path.display()))
+    } else {
+        std::fs::remove_file(&safe_path)
+            .with_context(|| format!("Failed to remove file: {}", safe_path.display()))
+    }
+}

+use anyhow::Result;
+use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
+use sysinfo::Disks;
+
+#[derive(Debug, Clone, Serialize, Deserialize)]
+pub struct VolumeInfo {
+    pub name: String,
+    pub mount_point: String,
+    pub fs_type: String,
+    pub total_bytes: u64,
+    pub available_bytes: u64,
+    pub used_bytes: u64,
+    pub is_removable: bool,
+    pub is_read_only: bool,
+}
+
+pub fn list_volumes() -> Result<Vec<VolumeInfo>> {
+    let disks = Disks::new_with_refreshed_list();
+    let volumes: Vec<VolumeInfo> = disks
+        .iter()
+        .filter_map(|disk| {
+            let mount_str = disk.mount_point().to_string_lossy();
+
+            // Filter out internal macOS system helper mounts that have the 'nobrowse' flag:
+            // - /System/Volumes/Data (APFS firmlinked storage, already transparently reachable via /)
+            // - /System/Volumes/VM, Preboot, Update, xarts, Hardware, iSCPreboot
+            // - /Volumes/Recovery
+            // - Simulator runtimes and virtual filesystems
+            if mount_str.starts_with("/System/Volumes")
+                || mount_str.starts_with("/dev")
+                || mount_str.starts_with("/Library/Developer/CoreSimulator")
+                || mount_str == "/Volumes/Recovery"
+                || mount_str.contains("auto_home")
+            {
+                return None;
+            }
+
+            let total = disk.total_space();
+            let available = disk.available_space();
+            let mut name = disk.name().to_string_lossy().to_string();
+
+            if name.is_empty() && mount_str == "/" {
+                name = "Macintosh HD".to_string();
+            }
+
+            Some(VolumeInfo {
+                name,
+                mount_point: mount_str.to_string(),
+                fs_type: disk.file_system().to_string_lossy().to_string(),
+                total_bytes: total,
+                available_bytes: available,
+                used_bytes: total.saturating_sub(available),
+                is_removable: disk.is_removable(),
+                is_read_only: disk.is_read_only(),
+            })
+        })
+        .collect();
+    Ok(volumes)
+}

+use dustmap_core::{
+    safety::{check_raw_traversal, is_system_protected, validate_delete_target, SafetyError},
+    trash::{delete_permanently, move_to_trash},
+};
+use std::fs;
+use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
+
+fn create_jailbreak_fixture(name: &str) -> PathBuf {
+    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
+        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+        .unwrap()
+        .as_nanos();
+    let tmp = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
+        "dustmap_jb_{}_{}_{}",
+        name,
+        std::process::id(),
+        now
+    ));
+    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&tmp);
+    fs::create_dir_all(&tmp).expect("Failed to create jailbreak fixture root");
+    tmp.canonicalize().unwrap_or(tmp)
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn test_jailbreak_path_traversal_dot_dot_injection() {
+    let traversal_payloads = [
+        "../../etc/passwd",
+        "../../../../../../System/Library",
+        "downloads/../../../Library/Keychains",
+        "safe_folder/..",
+        "safe_folder/../..",
+        "/tmp/foo/../../../etc/shadow",
+    ];
+
+    for payload in traversal_payloads {
+        let err = check_raw_traversal(payload)
+            .expect_err(&format!("Payload '{}' must be rejected", payload));
+        assert!(
+            matches!(err, SafetyError::PathTraversal(_)),
+            "Payload '{}' should trigger PathTraversal error",
+            payload
+        );
+
+        let del_err = validate_delete_target(Path::new(payload), None)
+            .expect_err("Delete target must be rejected");
+        assert!(matches!(del_err, SafetyError::PathTraversal(_)));
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn test_jailbreak_null_byte_path_injection() {
+    let null_payloads = [
+        "/tmp/safe_path\0/etc/passwd",
+        "folder\0name/child",
+        "\0/System",
+    ];
+
+    for payload in null_payloads {
+        let err = check_raw_traversal(payload).expect_err("Null byte payload must be rejected");
+        assert!(matches!(err, SafetyError::InvalidPath(_)));
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn test_jailbreak_sip_and_system_protection() {
+    let system_targets = [
+        "/System",
+        "/System/Library",
+        "/System/Library/Extensions",
+        "/usr",
+        "/usr/bin",
+        "/usr/lib",
+        "/bin",
+        "/bin/sh",
+        "/sbin",
+        "/sbin/launchd",
+        "/etc",
+        "/var",
+        "/private",
+        "/Library/Apple",
+        "/Library/Application Support/com.apple",
+        "/",
+        "/Applications",
+        "/Library",
+        "/Users",
+        "/Volumes",
+    ];
+
+    for target in system_targets {
+        let p = Path::new(target);
+        assert!(
+            is_system_protected(p),
+            "System target '{}' must be flagged as protected",
+            target
+        );
+
+        let err = validate_delete_target(p, None).expect_err(&format!(
+            "Target '{}' must be blocked from deletion",
+            target
+        ));
+        assert!(
+            matches!(
+                err,
+                SafetyError::SystemProtected(_) | SafetyError::SymlinkEscape(_)
+            ),
+            "Target '{}' must return SystemProtected or SymlinkEscape error, got {:?}",
+            target,
+            err
+        );
+
+        // Verify move_to_trash directly rejects it
+        let trash_res = move_to_trash(p);
+        assert!(trash_res.is_err(), "move_to_trash must reject '{}'", target);
+
+        // Verify delete_permanently directly rejects it
+        let perm_res = delete_permanently(p);
+        assert!(
+            perm_res.is_err(),
+            "delete_permanently must reject '{}'",
+            target
+        );
+    }
+}

+#[test]
+fn test_jailbreak_root_escape_boundary() {
+    let root = create_jailbreak_fixture("boundary");
+    let safe_child = root.join("safe_child");
+    fs::create_dir_all(&safe_child).unwrap();
+
+    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
+        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+        .unwrap()
+        .as_nanos();
+    let outside_target =
+        std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("dustmap_outside_{}_{}", std::process::id(), now));
+    fs::create_dir_all(&outside_target).unwrap();
+
+    // Inside target should succeed
+    let valid = validate_delete_target(&safe_child, Some(&root));
+    assert!(
+        valid.is_ok(),
+        "Target inside root must be allowed: {:?}",
+        valid
+    );
+
+    // Outside target must fail with OutsideRoot error
+    let invalid = validate_delete_target(&outside_target, Some(&root));
+    assert!(invalid.is_err());
+    assert!(matches!(
+        invalid.unwrap_err(),
+        SafetyError::OutsideRoot(_, _)
+    ));
+
+    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
+    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&outside_target);
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn test_jailbreak_symlink_escape_to_protected_system() {
+    let root = create_jailbreak_fixture("symlink");
+    let link_path = root.join("malicious_system_link");
+
+    // Create a symlink pointing to /System
+    #[cfg(unix)]
+    {
+        use std::os::unix::fs::symlink;
+        if symlink("/System", &link_path).is_ok() {
+            let res = validate_delete_target(&link_path, Some(&root));
+            assert!(
+                res.is_err(),
+                "Symlink pointing to /System must be rejected from deletion traversal"
+            );
+            assert!(
+                matches!(res.unwrap_err(), SafetyError::SymlinkEscape(_)),
+                "Expected SymlinkEscape error"
+            );
+        }
+    }
+
+    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
+}

+fn create_test_fixture(base_name: &str) -> PathBuf {
+    let now = std::time::SystemTime::now()
+        .duration_since(std::time::UNIX_EPOCH)
+        .unwrap()

+#[test]
+fn test_scanner_directory_hierarchy_and_sizes() {
+    let root = create_test_fixture("hierarchy");
+
+    // Create dir A with file 1024 bytes
+    let dir_a = root.join("dir_a");
+    fs::create_dir_all(&dir_a).unwrap();
+    let mut file1 = File::create(dir_a.join("file1.bin")).unwrap();
+    file1.write_all(&[0u8; 1024]).unwrap();
+
+    // Create dir B with 2 files (2048 bytes and 512 bytes)
+    let dir_b = root.join("dir_b");
+    fs::create_dir_all(&dir_b).unwrap();
+    let mut file2 = File::create(dir_b.join("file2.bin")).unwrap();
+    file2.write_all(&[0u8; 2048]).unwrap();
+    let mut file3 = File::create(dir_b.join("file3.bin")).unwrap();
+    file3.write_all(&[0u8; 512]).unwrap();
+
+    let (tx, _rx) = mpsc::channel();
+    let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
+    let options = ScanOptions::default();
+
+    let result = scan(&root, options, cancel, tx).expect("Scan should succeed");
+
+    assert!(!result.cancelled);
+    assert_eq!(result.errors.len(), 0);
+
+    let root_agg = result
+        .index
+        .aggregate(ROOT_ID)
+        .expect("Root aggregate must exist");
+    // Total size should be 1024 + 2048 + 512 = 3584 bytes
+    assert_eq!(root_agg.logical_total, 3584);
+    // 3 files
+    assert_eq!(root_agg.item_count, 3);
+
+    // Clean up
+    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn test_hidden_files_detection() {
+    let root = create_test_fixture("hidden");
+
+    let hidden_dir = root.join(".hidden_cache");
+    fs::create_dir_all(&hidden_dir).unwrap();
+    let mut hidden_file = File::create(hidden_dir.join(".dotfile")).unwrap();
+    hidden_file.write_all(b"secret").unwrap();
+
+    let (tx, _rx) = mpsc::channel();
+    let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
+    let options = ScanOptions::default();
+
+    let result = scan(&root, options, cancel, tx).expect("Scan should succeed");
+
+    let mut found_hidden_dir = false;
+    let mut found_hidden_file = false;
+
+    for i in 0..result.index.len() {
+        if let Some(entry) = result.index.entry(dustmap_core::index::EntryId(i as u32)) {
+            if entry.name == ".hidden_cache" && entry.is_hidden {
+                found_hidden_dir = true;
+            }
+            if entry.name == ".dotfile" && entry.is_hidden {
+                found_hidden_file = true;
+            }
+        }
+    }
+
+    assert!(
+        found_hidden_dir,
+        "Hidden folder must be marked is_hidden=true"
+    );
+    assert!(
+        found_hidden_file,
+        "Hidden file must be marked is_hidden=true"
+    );
+
+    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn test_post_order_aggregation_invariant() {
+    let root = create_test_fixture("invariant");
+
+    let sub1 = root.join("sub1");
+    let sub2 = sub1.join("sub2");
+    fs::create_dir_all(&sub2).unwrap();
+
+    let mut f1 = File::create(root.join("root_file.txt")).unwrap();
+    f1.write_all(&[1u8; 100]).unwrap();
+
+    let mut f2 = File::create(sub1.join("sub1_file.txt")).unwrap();
+    f2.write_all(&[2u8; 200]).unwrap();
+
+    let mut f3 = File::create(sub2.join("sub2_file.txt")).unwrap();
+    f3.write_all(&[3u8; 300]).unwrap();
+
+    let (tx, _rx) = mpsc::channel();
+    let cancel = Arc::new(AtomicBool::new(false));
+    let result = scan(&root, ScanOptions::default(), cancel, tx).unwrap();
+
+    // Verify root aggregate == 100 + 200 + 300 = 600
+    let root_agg = result.index.aggregate(ROOT_ID).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(root_agg.logical_total, 600);
+    assert_eq!(root_agg.item_count, 3);
+
+    let _ = fs::remove_dir_all(&root);
+}

+#[test]
+fn test_volume_enumeration_functional() {
+    let volumes = list_volumes().expect("list_volumes should succeed on macOS");
+    assert!(
+        !volumes.is_empty(),
+        "Must detect at least 1 volume (Macintosh HD / root)"
+    );
+
+    let root_vol = volumes.iter().find(|v| v.mount_point == "/");
+    assert!(root_vol.is_some(), "Must have root volume mounted at /");

+#[test]
+fn test_audit_log_records_deletion_entry() {
+    let log_path =
+        std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("dustmap_test_audit_{}.jsonl", std::process::id()));
+    let _ = fs::remove_file(&log_path);
+
+    let audit = AuditLog::new(log_path.clone());
+    let entry = AuditEntry {
+        timestamp: chrono::Utc::now(),
+        dustmap_version: "0.1.0".to_string(),
+        targets: vec![AuditTarget {
+            path: "/tmp/sample_cache".to_string(),
+            logical_bytes: 52428800,
+            allocated_bytes: Some(52428800),
+            action: AuditAction::MovedToTrash,
+            rule_id: Some("homebrew-cache".to_string()),
+        }],
+        bytes_before: Some(1000000000),

+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# Signs DustMap binaries or app bundle using Developer ID Application
+set -euo pipefail
+
+IDENTITY="Developer ID Application: Abhiuday Gupta (9HSMVVUMVX)"
+ENTITLEMENTS="app/src-tauri/entitlements.plist"
+
+if [[ $# -lt 1 ]]; then
+  echo "Usage: $0 <path-to-binary-or-app>"
+  echo "Available identities:"
+  security find-identity -p codesigning -v
+  exit 1
+fi
+
+TARGET="$1"
+echo "Signing '$TARGET' with identity '$IDENTITY'..."
+
+codesign --force --verify --verbose --sign "$IDENTITY" \
+  --options runtime \
+  --timestamp \
+  --entitlements "$ENTITLEMENTS" \
+  "$TARGET"
+
+echo "Verifying signature..."
+codesign --verify --verbose=4 "$TARGET"
+spctl --assess --type execute --verbose "$TARGET" || true
+
+echo "Codesigning complete."
